Suppose a person who thinks the world is flat. He (ok, or she) starts walking in a straight line. Eventually, he will find that he is at the same place he started out. He does not understand this, but it makes him wonder - could there be a faster way to travel in this flat world?

Suppose his path from start to finish is 40.000km. If he walks 1 km per hour, he will have to travel for 39.999 hours to get 39.999 km away from home. But, by using the very phenomenon that is a mystery to him, namely the curvature of his supposed flat earth, he can be home in 1 hour.

In our world, some scientists think that black holes exert so much gravity on their surroundings that space (actually - spacetime) around and in a black hole is curved. We can't understand that, because we are used to a 3D universe (our 'flat earth'). But if spacetime is curved in 4D, it just might be possible to travel 39.999 light years in a straight line, and be only 1 light year away from home - if you find the black hole that closes the spacetime loop that is.
